ev.q: The results indicated that nationwide, 12.9% of all high school students had ever been tested for HIV.
Overall, the prevalence of HIV testing was higher among female students (14.8%) than male students (11.1%; p<0.001),
nationwide, 12.9% of students had ever been tested for HIV (excluding tests for blood donation)
Overall, the prevalence of HIV testing was higher among female students (14.8%) than male students (11.1%; p<0.001),
The prevalence of HIV testing increased with increasing grade among non-Hispanic white female students (p<0.001)
Nonsignificant (p≥0.05) trend by grade using Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel trend test.
The 2007 national survey obtained cross-sectional data representative of public- and private-school students in grades 9--12
YRBS, a component of CDC's Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System, estimates the prevalence of health risk behaviors among high school students

methods_quotes.q: data were weighted to adjust for nonresponse and oversampling of black and Hispanic students
Analyses were conducted on weighted data using statistical software to account for the complex sample design
T-tests were used to determine statistically significant differences in HIV testing by sex, race/ethnicity
The Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel trend test was used to determine statistically significant differences in HIV testing by grade and age
Nonsignificant (p≥0.05) trend by grade using Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel trend test.
